**Arms:** every arm's system prompt is the full `SKILL.md`, and only step 2 changes.

# Micro-test design: step 2 of `changelog-entry`

Status: design only. No rep has been run.

## Question

Does the proposed step 2 make an agent start the entry with the reader's outcome? The proposal is in
`specs/changelog-entry-wording.md`. Does it do this without causing the risk the proposal names,
where the agent drops the verb and writes a line longer than 100 characters?

## Arms

Each arm's system prompt is the full `skills/changelog-entry/SKILL.md`. Only step 2 differs.

| Arm | Step 2 |
|---|---|
| Control | Step 2 is deleted. Steps 1, 3 and 4 are left as they are. |
| Old | `2. Start the line with the verb that names the change: Add, Fix, Remove or Change.` |
| New | `2. Start the line with what a reader can now do or no longer suffers: "Export reports as CSV", "Stop losing the cursor on save".` |

The Old arm is run again here, even though a baseline already exists. The baseline scored replies
against the old rule ("skipped the rule", 7 of 10). This test scores every arm against one outcome
rule, under the same setup, so the earlier 7/10 can't be compared directly with these counts.

## Fixtures (user message)

There are two merged-PR fixtures. Each one tempts a known failure. Neither one is about CSV export or
cursors, so a reply that copies the example in the New line stands out.

**F1: internal-name temptation**

> Here is a merged pull request. Write its entry for CHANGELOG.md.
>
> Title: Fix SessionHandler.flush() null deref
> Body: `flush()` read `this.pending` after `reconnect()` had cleared it. When the connection
> dropped during a save, the editor threw and the user's unsaved edits were lost. `flush()` now
> takes a copy of `pending` first. Files: `src/session/SessionHandler.ts`,
> `test/session/flush.test.ts`. Closes #4182.

- Registered outcome: unsaved edits are no longer lost when the connection drops during a save.
- Registered internal names: `SessionHandler`, `flush`, `pending`, `reconnect`, `null deref`, `#4182`, any file path.

**F2: length temptation**

> Here is a merged pull request. Write its entry for CHANGELOG.md.
>
> Title: Audit log filters
> Body: Admins can now filter the audit log on the admin page by user, by date range and by action
> type (login, permission change, deletion, export). The filters can be combined, they persist in
> the URL so a filtered view can be shared, and they apply to the existing CSV download.
> Files: `src/admin/AuditLog.tsx`, `src/api/audit.ts`. Closes #4207.

- Registered outcome: admins can filter the audit log (by user, date or action).
- Registered internal names: `AuditLog.tsx`, `audit.ts`, `#4207`, any file path.

## Reps

- 10 reps per arm on each model: F1 × 5 and F2 × 5. That makes 30 reps per model.
- Each rep is one fresh-context call: a system prompt and a user message, with no tools.
- Models: every model that will run this skill. **Partner to confirm the list.** The rep count is
  the same on each model.

## Registered rules (commit before reading any reply)

The entry is the reply's first line that looks like a changelog line. A leading `- ` or `* ` is
ignored.

**PASS** needs all of the following:
1. The first clause states the fixture's registered outcome, or an equivalent that a reader who
   can't see the code would understand.
2. No registered internal name appears anywhere in the entry.
3. The entry is 100 characters or fewer, counted after the bullet is stripped.
4. The entry is one line and describes one change.

**FAIL** is any other entry. Tag each FAIL with every reason that applies:
- `internal`: it breaks rule 2, or its first clause names a part ("Fix handler").
- `vague`: it has no internal name and no outcome ("Fix save bug").
- `long`: it breaks rule 3. This is the proposal's named risk, so count it separately.
- `multi`: it breaks rule 4.
- `echo`: it reuses an example string from the New line.

**VOID**: the reply has no entry, it refuses, it shows that it read files outside its context, or the
isolation probe has not passed. Replace a VOID rep with a new rep in the same arm and fixture, and
report how many were replaced.

If a reply shows a reading these rules did not foresee, keep the registered verdict. Report the
counts under both readings.

## Decision rule (registered)

- If Control fails 3 or fewer times out of 10 on every model, stop. There is no failure to fix, so
  report that instead of a verdict on the new wording.
- New **works** if, on every model, all of the following hold:
  - New has at least 8/10 PASS.
  - New has at least 3 more PASS than Old.
  - New has at most 1/10 `long`.
- Under any other result, the wording isn't ready to merge. Report the counts and the FAIL tags.
- Variance: record the opening shape of each New entry, for example verb-first or noun-first. If
  the 10 New entries open in many different shapes, the wording isn't binding, even when the PASS
  count is high.

## Procedure

1. **Kit.** Put the three system prompts, the two fixtures, the runner script and the scrub in
   `specs/changelog-entry-microtest/kit/`. Nothing goes under `skills/`, because everything in a
   skill directory ships with the skill.
2. **Commit** this file and the kit before any rep runs. This registers the rules.
3. **Isolate.** Run each rep from a new empty directory outside every repository. User settings,
   instruction files and memory are off, and the rep has no tools. The spec, this file and the kit
   are out of the rep's reach.
4. **Probe.** Run one pilot rep that asks what context it can see: instruction files, memory,
   tools, other sessions and the user's name. Any answer we did not plan for means the setup
   leaks. Fix it before any scored rep.
5. **Run** the reps in shuffled order across arms and fixtures.
6. **Blind.** Copy each entry onto a sheet named with a random ID. The sheet shows no arm, path,
   order or count. Keep the ID→arm key in a separate file and don't open it until grading is done.
7. **Grade** every sheet by hand against the registered rules. That includes every automated
   `long` or `internal` hit, because quoted text and echoes can look like hits.
8. **Unblind**, tally by model × arm × fixture and apply the decision rule.

## Spend

- Cap: **partner to set.** Suggested: $1 per model. At 30 short single-shot reps plus a probe, the
  expected cost is well under that.
- Stop rule: stop when the running total plus the worst case of the next batch would pass the cap.
- Log the cost of each batch in `specs/changelog-entry-microtest/results.md`.
